subject: Warning while using random values OR why I didn't get the same results in shiny and R console

messages.author: 8899033a1963ffa1
messages.subject: Warning while using random values OR why I didn't get the same results in shiny and R console
parts:
I developed a code involving random values with control of the random seed in the R console, and couldn't get the same results within my Shiny app. It took me a while to find out that reactivity and lazy-evaluation led to the error. It seems obvious to me now. This post may help.

Here is a minimal example
The code could be

test <- function(a){
  set.seed(9380297)
  # Some code here involving a such as
  print(a)
  # more code
  return(paste(LETTERS[sample(x = 25,size=5,rep=TRUE)],collapse = ""))
}
a <- runif(1)
test(a)
 
leading to 
[1] 0.3416042
[1] "HELLO"


In a Shiny app, using the same function test

library(shiny)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    actionButton("Button","Run"),
    verbatimTextOutput("out") 
    ),
  server = function(input, output) {
   
    a <- reactive({input$Button
                  runif(1)})
   
    output$out <- renderPrint(test(a()))
  }
)

won't lead you to the same results. It's obvious since a is evaluated only when used, and "shift" the pseudo random values. It took me a while because "a" was used in the middle of a long function.

Solutions are to evaluate the parameters before setting the random seed (beginning of your function) or to set the random seed just before you use it...

test <- function(a){
  #If you are sure you'll need a, you can evaluate it at the beginning of the function  set.seed(9380297)
  a
  set.seed(9380297)
  # Some code here involving a such as
  print(a)
  # more code
  return(paste(LETTERS[sample(x = 25,size=5,rep=TRUE)],collapse = ""))
}
